source_readme.method: Per-observation 1 MHz histograms of existing detector hit counts; not original telescope powers
source_readme.threshold_selection: The author selected the energy-detection statistic threshold 4096 to obtain spectral occupancy similar to turboSETI.

source_code_provenance.supports: Stores os.path.basename(.dat path) in filename and bin_edges[j] as histogram column labels. S-band notch option excludes labels 2300 through2360 inclusive.

Stores observation folder basename in filename, lower bin edges as labels, S band edges1800..2801 with width1. Notch option excludes labels2300 through2360 inclusive. README states4096 for published dataset; code default2048 is not treated as its applied threshold.

identity_matching.raw: Exact filename string, without any normalization.
identity_matching.canonical: Remove one terminal literal '.dat' from turboSETI filename only; energy_detection filename unchanged. No other stripping, case folding, stem matching or fuzzy matching.
identity_matching.justification: Pinned producer code stores turboSETI .dat basename and energy-detection observation folder basename.
identity_matching.no_match_behavior: Keep unpaired per-dataset summaries and record no exact/canonical pairing; paired fractions null.

analysis.neighborhood_choice: Fixed from prior BU/BV/BW search near2298.937–2301.844MHz, before reading new histogram rows; no selection by peaks.
analysis.notch_rule: Flag labels2300..2360 as the source code's notch region; retain all bins. Do not infer clean sky, receiver sensitivity or physical notch edges from low counts.

interpretation_limits: Counts are derived detector outputs; thresholds and algorithms differ, so occupancy differences do not rank detector performance.
Similar occupancy between the methods is not independent validation: the energy-detection threshold was selected to obtain comparable spectral occupancy.
Rows may be correlated and exposure/validity masks are unavailable. Denominators are published rows, not independently qualified observing time.
Zero counts can reflect notches, missing frequency coverage, dropped nodes or preprocessing rather than a quiet band.
Date coverage is the author's dataset description, not an independently decoded timestamp validation.
Published code documents interpretation; the exact historical producer execution and options are not reconstructed.
No new raw SETI searches, candidate qualification, calibrated sensitivity, FAP or original survey coverage.
